descriptionHtml:
Case priority: P1 · our extension of a stated behaviour · ours: failed send, retry, double tap, sender clock two days off.

Bug B18 · S1 · known

Many dates and times follow the device clock instead of server time (UAT 3.8): 'NEW TODAY', admit date, vitals date, task done time, transcript date; with a phone two days slow a held drug is stamped two days back and the next cleanup deletes it

Tickets: TFA-92584 ready for qa (UAT 3.8); TFA-92597 ready for qa (R6); TFA-92579 AC 3/4 ready for qa (NEW TODAY); TFA-94745 ready for qa (draft restore) · counts as a QA bug: yes · found on: local

Note: Root cause known (Daniela asked for server time on 10-03); the deleted drug, missing badge and wrong draft restore are new symptoms. TC-16/S18 (UAT 3.8, one device set to the wrong date): a phone a day ahead files its bedside line in a row dated tomorrow on the shared record, and the next write from a correctly clocked device lists the lines before it twice (the transcript archive trusts the device date). Which calendar day a correct device should use when its local day and the server's UTC day differ is the open question Q9 (D10); TC-16/S25 passed otherwise. Review 2026-10-14 (TFA-92579/92584): a browser whose day is ahead writes the badge roll back to the server, and every device shows Follow-up, with the matching template and billing family (TC-01/S08, TC-20/S20a; TFA-92584 AC 8). The failing cell of TC-25/S24a is the card's NEW TODAY, which compares addedAt with the device's date (PatientCard.tsx:154-156). EFS/S28 (a)(b) restore drafts by the device date (TFA-94745); (c), an old draft put in today's box, is B13's. Review 2026-10-15 (TFA-94514): the analytics day is the device date too (pilotUsageEvents / pilotDailyRounding use localDay()): a phone 3 days ahead files its rows under its own day, and an encounter across the phone midnight is split over two days and never timed (OAT-06/S10). Re-test 2026-10-16 (TC-21/S26, 25acd727): a browser two days ahead writes the badge roll with its own future day (encTypeDay 2026-10-19) to the shared record, so the correct-clock browser shows Follow-up too. Re-test 2026-10-20 on 8b4be94a: changed: task done time and Important Points now use server time (TC-22/S23, TC-12/S23, TC-07/S28 stamp); still device time: Tomorrow's Pre-Round Summary edit (TC-17/S25), task screen header date (TC-07/S28), handoff title date (TC-08/S20), medicationsUpdatedAt (TC-19/S19), NEW TODAY (TC-01/S08), completeEncounter day (OAT-06/S10).

Other cases of the same bug (counted once): TC-01/S08, TC-10/S22, TC-12/S23, TC-19/S19, TC-22/S23, TC-25/S24a, TC-02/S13b, EFS/S28, TC-16/S18, TC-06/S19, OAT-06/S10, TC-06/S23, TC-21/S22, TC-25/S24b, TC-19/S23, TC-21/S26, TC-17/S25, TC-07/S28

Approach · TC-08 Handoff Summary · S20 Send under faults: a failed send, a retry, a double tap and a sender clock two days off — exactly one record each, with the server's time

UAT steps / ticket ACs covered:

  • U11 The record's timestamp follows the server clock (3.8): a sender device with a wrong date or time zone does not change the recorded send time. (UAT 3.8; UAT TC-08) — gate: blocked: TFA-92586 ready for pr
  • U6 Every sent handoff leaves a persistent record (sender, recipient, timestamp) that both the sender and the recipient can retrieve. (UAT TC-08; TFA-92586 AC 8) — gate: blocked: TFA-92586 ready for pr
  • U4 The sending physician can edit the generated handoff before sending, and the recipient, retrieving it from their own account, sees exactly the edited text. (UAT TC-08; TFA-92586 AC 4) — gate: blocked: TFA-92586 ready for pr
  • U5 The handoff is generated and delivered entirely in-app, only to a signed-in, valid Round Companion recipient (another physician's account), never to an arbitrary email address; … (UAT TC-08; TFA-92586 AC 6; TFA-92586 AC 7) — gate: blocked: TFA-92586 ready for pr
  • U8 No email client opens, no mailto: link fires, and there is no email or external-share path for a handoff under any condition, failures included (the After-Pilot no-PHI email notification is absent to … (UAT TC-08; TFA-92586 AC 6) — gate: blocked: TFA-92586 ready for pr

Test design technique: Error guessing (error-guessing) — Go straight for the places most likely to break (failures, double clicks, two tabs, a wrong clock, injected instructions).

Given Sender and a seeded @roundai.test recipient, each in their own browser context; the sender's context runs its clock two days ahead in another time zone; S01 census

When Sender opens Handoff → Send to…, adds 'QA-EDIT-F5 failure check' to the text and picks the recipient; the runner makes the first handoffs:send fail at the Convex socket; the sender presses Send, then presses Send again; then the sender sends a second handoff with a double-click on Send; …

Then After the failed send: the dialog is still open with the edited text, no 'Sent to' label, no new Sent or Received row, and no mailto:/email/share fallback; after the retry: exactly one Received row; after the double-click: exactly one more; every record's sentAt is an ISO-8601 time inside the runner's own clock window for that send, not two days ahead; …

Pass rule (oracle, excerpt): Probe assertions: the editor value still contains QA-EDIT-F5 after the failure; no 'Sent to ' text; row counts 0 after the failure, 1 after the retry, +1 after the double-click (never +2); during the failure the page has no 'mailto:', 'Email', 'Share', no window.open and no navigation away; …

Where it ran: local newspec-c (new Playwright specs); test method FAULT · Fault injection; lane planned in the matrix: browser agent (automated)

S20 is our own case number (its number in the coverage matrix cases/TC-08.matrix.json), not a step number of the UAT document.

Triage (2026-10-14): 0 rows; the triage is about a test issue and the result shown here is a full pass, so its status is kept.

Environment: local — main e02167f → 8b4be94a (10-20 re-run), local stack (not a deployed build); run folder runs/2026-10-14-local, lane newspec-c.

Test method: FAULT · Fault injection; secondary: MULTI · Multi-device / multi-account — as classified in cases/test-methods.json, which says it runs on local; Source: newspec-c.
